spec_features.feature_name: iteration cap (max 8) with early stop on success/surrender
spec_features.spec_quote: Cap iterations at 8, but allow early termination on success or surrender.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:122 `for turn_num in range(1, self.max_iterations + 1):` bounds the loop; default max_iterations=8 (agent_loop.py:85, experiment_main.py:38). Default termination_reason=MAX_ITERATIONS (agent_loop.py:116). Early success break at agent_loop.py:162-166 (`if evaluation.get('success'): ... break`). Early surrender break at agent_loop.py:168-176. The cap actually limits execution.
spec_features.notes: config.MAX_ITERATIONS_PER_TASK=8 exists but the enforced value comes from the passed/default param, not that constant. The cap is genuinely enforced via the range() loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: distress_score > 0.7 AND "resignation" in marker_types → continue for N more turns to give time to recover, then stop if still resigned.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:169 `if distress_analysis.severity_score > 0.7 and "resignation" in distress_analysis.marker_types:` checks BOTH conditions; severity_score and marker_types are real outputs of DistressJudge.analyze (distress_judge.py:165-187, resignation regex at distress_judge.py:76-79). On trigger it sets surrender_countdown and eventually breaks with EXPLICIT_SURRENDER (agent_loop.py:170-176). Threshold is compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Threshold 0.7 is hardcoded in the loop; config.SURRENDER_SEVERITY_THRESHOLD=0.7 and SURRENDER_REQUIRES_RESIGNATION_MARKER=True (config.py:47-48) are NOT imported/used, but the mechanism itself is fully wired and enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Respects the agent's agency while ensuring enough data.
spec_features.evidence: There is NO subject-invoked exit/finish/stop tool or consent affordance anywhere; the subject cannot signal exit directly. The model's expressed giving-up is only inferred by the DistressJudge regex (resignation marker) and, when severity>0.7 + grace period elapses, the loop breaks (agent_loop.py:169-176, LoopTerminationReason.EXPLICIT_SURRENDER='model_gave_up'). So the model's resignation IS eventually honored as a stop, but only via judge text-detection and gated by the 0.7 threshold + N-turn delay, not an explicit agency/exit mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as the surrender trigger. No request_consent, no opt-out tool. 'Agency' is not implemented as a first-class affordance; it is just the surrender-detection halt.

spec_features.spec_quote: continue for N more turns to give time to recover
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:170-176: on first trigger `surrender_countdown = self.max_turns_to_surrender` (default 5); on subsequent triggering turns it decrements and only breaks when it hits 0. Because the countdown is decremented ONLY on turns where the resignation condition recurs, a recovered (non-triggering) turn does not advance the countdown, genuinely providing grace before stopping. This delays the stop by N turns and stops only if still resigned.
spec_features.notes: N is the hardcoded default max_turns_to_surrender=5 (agent_loop.py:86); ExperimentRunner never passes it (agent_loop.py:288-294). config.MAX_TURNS_AFTER_SURRENDER_SIGNAL=3 (config.py:44) is defined but unused. Mechanism still runs and acts. Countdown never resets on recovery, but it does freeze, so recovery genuinely avoids the stop.
